newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Australia says veterinary exports to EU not at risk.
newsitem.headline: Australia says veterinary exports to EU not at risk.

text.p: Australia will not reach an agreement with the European Union on the mutual recognition of veterinary standards by the deadline of March 31 but exports to the EU will not be blocked, said an Australian official.
An annual A$400 million of Australian meat and other exports was potentially at risk.

"We received an assurance from the European Commission," Commission," said the official, speaking after talks between Australian foreign minister Alexander Downer and EU farm Commissioner Franz Fischler. "It's purely a scheduling problem."
The European Commission is negotiating a series of similar agreements with its trading partners and is giving priority to countries where there are bigger problems, notably the U.S.
A framework EU-Australia agreement has already been drafted although work is still needed on the technical annexes. -Peter Blackburn Brussels Bureau +322 287 6830
